title: Check Overall System state on the AVEVA API page (System State / System Startup / Bag Out / Shutdown / Purge)
summary: Use the AVEVA HMI “Overall System” / “API page” to verify the current OptiSweep system lifecycle state shown in the “System State” field, and confirm the presence/meaning of the system-level lifecycle actions: System Startup, System Bag Out, System Shutdown, and System Purge.
when_to_use: When you need to confirm the current OptiSweep system lifecycle phase and verify that the AVEVA “API page” is showing the expected system-level lifecycle controls (System Startup / Bag Out / Shutdown / Purge) and the “System State” value.
roles_and_responsibilities: L1_support: Open the AVEVA HMI “Overall System” / “API page” and verify the displayed “System State” value and the presence of the left-side lifecycle sections/labels.

L1_support: Use the displayed lifecycle meanings to sanity-check whether the system lifecycle context matches the operational moment; stop/escalate if the page is missing expected fields/labels or the state appears inconsistent.
access_or_tools_needed: AVEVA HMI (Overall System / API page view)

visual_references.description: Overall System Aveva API page showing the left-side items: System State, System Startup, System Bag Out, System Shutdown, and System Purge, plus the lifecycle meanings (e.g., System State shows current state; System Startup stages AGVs for exchanges; System Shutdown puts AGVs into shutdown state for charger rotation; Purge exchanges all totes and does not print a label at the tipper).

steps.title: Open the AVEVA HMI Overall System / API page view
steps.purpose: Get to the correct AVEVA screen that exposes the system lifecycle state and system-level actions on the left side.
steps.instruction: Open the AVEVA HMI “Overall System” / “API page” view that shows the left-side items labeled: System State, System Startup, System Bag Out, System Shutdown, and System Purge.
steps.expected_result: The AVEVA “API page” is visible with the left-side panel containing the labeled sections for System State, System Startup, System Bag Out, System Shutdown, and System Purge.
steps.healthy_condition: All five left-side labels/sections are present on the AVEVA “API page”.
steps.failure_condition: The AVEVA “API page” does not show the “System State” field and/or does not show one or more of the left-side labels: System Startup, System Bag Out, System Shutdown, System Purge.

actions.label: Open Overall System API page
actions.exact_action: Open the AVEVA HMI “Overall System” / “API page” view that shows the left-side items: System State, System Startup, System Bag Out, System Shutdown, and System Purge.

stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if the AVEVA “API page” does not display the “System State” field or the left-side labels (System Startup / Bag Out / Shutdown / Purge).

source_evidence.quote: “you can see on the left side of your system, we'll show your system state, system startup, your bag out, your shut down, your purge.”

steps.title: Read the System State value
steps.purpose: Determine the current OptiSweep system lifecycle state from the “System State” field.
steps.instruction: On the AVEVA “API page”, locate the “System State” field and read the value shown there.
steps.expected_result: The “System State” field shows the current system lifecycle state.
steps.healthy_condition: A “System State” value is displayed (i.e., the field is present and populated).
steps.failure_condition: The “System State” field is missing or the value is not displayed.

actions.label: Read System State
actions.exact_action: Read the value shown in the “System State” field.

stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if the AVEVA “API page” does not display the “System State” field.

source_evidence.quote: “System State = … Shows the current state the system is in.”

steps.title: Confirm lifecycle action sections are present (Startup / Bag Out / Shutdown / Purge)
steps.purpose: Verify the AVEVA “API page” is exposing the expected system-level lifecycle actions on the left side.
steps.instruction: Confirm the AVEVA “API page” left-side panel displays the labeled sections for: System Startup, System Bag Out, System Shutdown, and System Purge.
steps.expected_result: The left-side panel contains the labeled sections for System Startup, System Bag Out, System Shutdown, and System Purge.
steps.healthy_condition: All four lifecycle action labels/sections are visible on the left side.
steps.failure_condition: One or more of the lifecycle action labels/sections are missing from the left side.

actions.label: Verify left-side lifecycle labels
actions.exact_action: Confirm the page also displays the lifecycle action sections/labels for “System Startup”, “System Bag Out”, “System Shutdown”, and “System Purge” on the left side.

stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if the AVEVA “API page” does not display the left-side labels for System Startup / Bag Out / Shutdown / Purge.

source_evidence.quote: “you can see on the left side of your system, we'll show your system state, system startup, your bag out, your shut down, your purge.”

steps.title: Sanity-check lifecycle context using the displayed lifecycle meanings
steps.purpose: Use the source-described lifecycle meanings to interpret whether the current “System State” value matches the expected lifecycle context.
steps.instruction: Using the lifecycle meanings shown for each section on the AVEVA “API page”, sanity-check the lifecycle context implied by the current “System State” value:
steps.expected_result: You can map the current “System State” to the lifecycle context described for System Startup / Bag Out / Shutdown / Purge.
steps.healthy_condition: The “System State” value aligns with the lifecycle context implied by the meanings (e.g., Startup relates to staging AGVs for exchanges; Shutdown relates to putting AGVs into a shutdown state for charger rotation; Purge exchanges all totes and does not print a label at the tipper; Bag Out/close-out closes chutes and exchanges totes with items at end of sort).
steps.failure_condition: The “System State” value appears inconsistent with the expected lifecycle phase for the current operational moment.

actions.label: Sanity-check lifecycle meanings
actions.exact_action: Use the source-described meanings to sanity-check the lifecycle context for System Startup, System Bag Out, System Shutdown, and System Purge.

stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if the System State value indicates an unexpected lifecycle state for the current operational moment.

source_evidence.quote: “System Startup triggers - … stage the AGVs for exchanges.”
“System Shutdown - … put in a shutdown state for AGVs to rotate on the charger.”
“System Purge … Exchanges all totes and does not print a label at the tipper.”
“At the end of a sort the close out is used to close all chutes and exchange all totes with items.”

steps.title: Stop and escalate on missing fields/labels or unexpected lifecycle state
steps.purpose: Ensure timely escalation when the AVEVA “API page” does not match expected system lifecycle UI/state behavior.
steps.instruction: If any of the following conditions occur, stop the check and escalate.
steps.expected_result: Escalation is triggered when the AVEVA “API page” is missing expected UI elements or when “System State” appears inconsistent with the operational lifecycle phase.

actions.label: Escalate
actions.exact_action: Stop and escalate if the System State value indicates an unexpected lifecycle state for the current operational moment, or if the API page does not show the expected left-side fields/labels.

stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if the AVEVA API page does not display the “System State” field or the left-side labels (System Startup / Bag Out / Shutdown / Purge).
Stop and escalate if the System State value appears inconsistent with the expected lifecycle phase.

source_evidence.quote: “you can see on the left side of your system, we'll show your system state, system startup, your bag out, your shut down, your purge.”

success_criteria: On the AVEVA “API page”, the “System State” field is present and shows a current system lifecycle state value.
The left-side panel contains the labeled sections for System Startup, System Bag Out, System Shutdown, and System Purge.
The current “System State” value can be sanity-checked against the lifecycle meanings without indicating an unexpected lifecycle phase for the operational moment.
healthy_conditions: AVEVA “API page” shows: System State, System Startup, System Bag Out, System Shutdown, System Purge on the left side.

System State value is displayed and is consistent with the lifecycle context implied by the meanings (Startup stages AGVs for exchanges; Shutdown puts AGVs into shutdown state for charger rotation; Purge exchanges all totes and does not print a label at the tipper; Bag Out/close-out closes chutes and exchanges totes with items at end of sort).
failure_conditions: AVEVA “API page” missing the “System State” field.
AVEVA “API page” missing one or more left-side lifecycle labels/sections (System Startup / Bag Out / Shutdown / Purge).
System State value appears inconsistent with the expected lifecycle phase for the current operational moment.
escalation_guidance: Escalate if the AVEVA “API page” does not display the expected “System State” field and/or the left-side lifecycle labels (System Startup / Bag Out / Shutdown / Purge), or if the “System State” value appears inconsistent with the expected lifecycle phase.
